ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$. Point $D$ is on side $AB$, and point $E$ is on side $BC$. After folding $\triangle BDE$ along line $DE$, point $B$ falls exactly on point $P$, which is on the extension of line segment $AC$. If $\angle APE=2\angle B$, what is the value of $\frac{BD}{AD}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's consider $Rt\triangle ABC$ where $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle A=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle APE=2\angle B=60^\circ$,\\
By folding, it is known that: $PD=BD\text{, }\angle DPE=\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle APD=\angle APE−\angle DPE=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADP=60^\circ+30^\circ=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \frac{PD}{AD}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BD}{AD}=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

Thus triangle ADP is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, with PD opposite 60° and AD opposite 30°, so PD/AD=√3. Since PD=BD, BD/AD=√3.
